subject: Discovery recap + scheduling next demo
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-14T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap + scheduling next demo

Hi Jordan — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary of discovery:
- Primary goal: reduce per-inference latency for Acme’s fleet management prompts while keeping unit cost under $0.003/token.
- Key constraints: EU data residency for telemetry, 99.9% uptime for customer-facing APIs, and a small on-prem inference footprint planned for Q4.
- Stakeholders: Platform (you), ML infra (Ken?), Security (TBD), and Product (Asha).

Proposed next step:
- Technical deep-dive + demo focused on model serving (KV cache, batching, and quantization options). ~45 minutes.
- I’d like to set up a short recurring demo cadence to ensure both the platform and ML infra can engage across time zones. Below are three rotation options I think will minimize friction across US / EU / APAC teams.

Rotation proposal (we can make this recurring and rotate weekly):
- Week A (US-friendly): Tue 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET / 18:00 BST (60 min)
- Week B (EU-friendly): Wed 09:30 BST / 10:30 CEST / 04:30 PT (60 min)
- Week C (APAC-friendly): Thu 10:00 AEST / 08:00 SGT / 18:00 BST (60 min)

If rotation is too heavy, alternative is a biweekly cadence that alternates US vs APAC/EU.

Attachments: I’ve attached a 1-page demo agenda and a draft mutual action plan to start populating roles/owners.

Can you confirm: (1) whether the rotating weekly cadence works for your leads, and (2) any blackout dates in May/June? If helpful, here’s a quick scheduler: https://cal.com/rachel-kim/redwood-demo

Thanks — I’ll loop in our infra lead for the deep-dive once we lock a slot.

—
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel — good recap. Quick notes from our side:
- Confirmed objectives. Latency and cost are primary; security questions will come from our Compliance team (I’ll intro them once we have a timeline).
- Team locations: Platform (London/UK), ML infra (Austin/US & Bangalore/APAC), Product (Boston/US). That distribution is why a rotating cadence makes sense.

Availability constraints:
- We have a company-wide offsite the week of 2026-06-07 — avoid that week.
- Prefer the EU-friendly slot for the first session so our Platform lead can attend live.

If you can propose two concrete dates (one EU-friendly and one US-friendly) I’ll scope which people can make each.

Jordan Ellis

Great — thanks for the constraints. Two concrete proposals below; I’ll hold both tentatively and you can tell me which to lock:

Option 1 (EU-friendly — preferred first session):
- Date: Wed 2026-05-20
- Time: 09:30 BST / 10:30 CEST / 04:30 PT
- Duration: 60 minutes

Option 2 (US-friendly):
- Date: Tue 2026-05-26
- Time: 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET / 18:00 BST
- Duration: 60 minutes

Rotation approach I’ll put in the recurring invite if both look good: start with Option 1, then rotate through the Week B / Week A / Week C pattern (APAC rotation to follow in week 3). We’ll run the repeated sessions for six weeks and reassess.

Agenda (attached short PDF):
- 00-10 min: short recap and success metrics
- 10-35 min: demo of serving runtime (KV cache + batching) with sample workload
- 35-50 min: infra/ops Q&A + region/fallback discussion
- 50-60 min: actions and owners (capture in MAP)

I’ve attached the agenda and an editable mutual action plan. I’ll also create the calendar invite and share a single doc for action items.

On invite owners: Sean will own the technical deep-dive; Marcus will take infra/region/ops questions. Sean — can you confirm you can lead the demo for Option 1?

—
Rachel
